articles.title: Brock Bowers Out 1-2 Games With Meniscus Trim
articles.description: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers is set to miss "a game or two" after undergoing a meniscus trim Tuesday, according to multiple reports. The procedure addressed an injury Bowers suffered during training camp, with the surgery having been scheduled last week. Bowers played through a PCL injury for much of last season, an issue that ultimately landed him on injured reserve for the final weeks of the year. His latest knee procedure marks a difficult start to the 2026 season and will complicate life for quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Raiders host the Miami Dolphins this weekend before traveling to face the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. With Bowers sidelined, tight ends Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas are set to take on larger roles. The team's receiving corps also includes Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor, Dareke Young and sixth-round pick Malik Benson. Las Vegas does hope to have running back Ashton Jeanty available for Sunday's game. Jeanty returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since suffering an ankle injury on Aug. 23, and coach Klint Kubiak had expressed optimism last week that Jeanty would be ready for the start of the regular season.
